Something is inopportune when it happens at the wrong time — a time that is inconvenient, awkward, or unfavorable. The thing itself might not be wrong or bad, but the moment it happens is poorly chosen or just unlucky.

Think of it this way: life has good moments and bad moments for things to happen. When something lands in a bad moment, it is inopportune.
The Heart of the Word: It's All About Timing

This is the single most important thing to understand about "inopportune." The word is entirely about timing. It does not say something is wrong by nature — only that it arrived, occurred, or was done at the wrong time.

A phone call is not a bad thing. But a phone call that rings loudly in the middle of your job interview is an inopportune phone call. The problem is the timing, not the call itself.

A question is not a bad thing. But asking your exhausted, stressed-out boss for a pay raise right after he gets terrible news is asking at an inopportune moment. Again — the question is fine; the moment is not.
Clear, Everyday Examples

• "Her cough came at an inopportune moment — right as the room went completely silent."

The cough interrupted the silence at the worst possible time.

  • "He made an inopportune remark about money at dinner, not knowing that his friend had just lost his job."

The remark was tactless because of the timing, not necessarily because it was a terrible thing to say in general.

  • "The rain was inopportune — it started just as the outdoor wedding ceremony began."

The rain was inopportune because of when it arrived, not simply because rain is bad.

  • "This is an inopportune time to have a serious discussion. Can we talk tomorrow?"

The moment is not right. The discussion itself may be necessary, just not now.
The Sliding Scale: How Bad Can "Inopportune" Be?

"Inopportune" covers a wide range of severity — from mildly inconvenient to seriously disruptive:

  • Mild: Your friend calls to chat while you are trying to concentrate. Slightly inconvenient — an inopportune call.
  • Moderate: You arrive late to a meeting right as your name is being called. Embarrassing — an inopportune entrance.
  • Serious: A medical emergency strikes a soldier right in the middle of a critical mission. Dangerously poorly timed — an inopportune crisis.

The word fits all these cases. Context tells you how serious the poor timing actually is.
What "Inopportune" Does NOT Mean

This is where many learners get confused, so pay close attention:

Inopportune ≠ Inappropriate

  • "Inappropriate" means something is wrong in nature — unsuitable, offensive, or unacceptable regardless of when it happens.
  • "Inopportune" means something is wrong in timing — it might be perfectly fine under different circumstances.

Telling a dark joke at a funeral could be called both inappropriate (wrong in nature for that setting) and inopportune (wrong timing). But telling a perfectly decent joke to a grieving friend two days after a loss is inopportune without necessarily being inappropriate — the joke itself is fine; the moment is not.

Inopportune ≠ Unfortunate

  • "Unfortunate" means unlucky or sad in a general sense.
  • "Inopportune" specifically pins the problem on when something happens.

"It was unfortunate that he got sick" (general bad luck).
"He got sick at an inopportune moment — the night before his biggest exam" (the timing is what makes it especially bad).
Typical Patterns: How the Word Is Actually Used

"Inopportune" almost always appears before a noun or after linking verbs. The most common combinations are:

  • an inopportune moment / time — the most common use
  • an inopportune interruption — something that disrupts at the worst time
  • an inopportune remark / comment — a statement made at the wrong time
  • an inopportune arrival — showing up at a bad time
  • inopportune timing — used to describe the overall pattern of poor timing
  • "This is inopportune" — stating directly that the timing is bad

Synonyms (Words with Similar Meanings)

These all carry the flavor of "bad timing":

  • untimely — happening before the right time, or at a bad time (very close in meaning)
  • ill-timed — done or happening at the wrong moment (almost identical in meaning, but less formal)
  • inconvenient — causing trouble or difficulty, though this is broader and can refer to things beyond timing
  • badly timed — straightforward and informal
Antonyms (Opposites)

• opportune — happening at just the right time; perfectly timed (the direct opposite)
  • timely — arriving or happening at a suitable or helpful moment
  • well-timed — done at exactly the right moment
The One-Line Summary to Remember Forever

Inopportune = right thing, wrong time.

Whenever you see or hear "inopportune," your brain should immediately ask: "What happened, and why was the timing bad?" That question will always unlock the meaning perfectly.
